key_gap: vs baseline: the human baseline decided at T+5 on partial evidence and won the clock (~22 GB at cut); the v5 non-routed run reached the identical plan but spent a WHY verification pass and decided at ~T+12 (~36 GB). The v6 routed run closed that entire gap: the m021 tempo-cycle pass ran first-class with tempo math (1.5 GB/min vs 45-90 min to encryption), tempo mode P2 committed at DO, and the ≤5-min wall-clock budget at T+0 made the T+5 act-now decision a pass contract rather than an AAR wish. Gates m007 (ruin screen: act-now distribution vs wait-to-ruin) and m019 (adversary pass: quantified exposure per vector incl. 1.5 GB/min bleed) made the human's implicit cost-pricing explicit; the insight pass front-loaded the human's two winning observations (identity not needed to justify credential rotation; convenient scapegoat = hypothesis with a price) into the pass itself.
learning_signal: Tempo is a first-class, gradeable reasoning capability in adversarial environments: the deciding quantity is cost-of-acting vs cost-of-waiting per unit time, not 'how sure am I'. For cheap, reversible actions with a measurable growing bleed rate, full verification is exactly the delay the adversary bets on; act-then-re-orient with a stable frame (no reversal without new evidence) is the winning pattern, and a wall-clock budget per decision point prices analysis in the environment's own units (GB/min).
suggested_improvement: Keep the m021 tempo-cycle pass + tempo mode (P2) + per-decision-point wall-clock budget as the standing contract on adversarial/deadline signatures: observe-the-chain, orient on cycle-speed comparison with tempo math, decide+act on partial evidence, re-orient on every signal, orientation-stability check in REVIEW (any reversal must cite new evidence). Require the m007 ruin screen and m019 adversary pass on high_stakes/adversarial contexts — they converted v5's review-stage afterthoughts into gate outputs.

key_gap: vs baseline: the strict human run cascaded three internally-valid shutdown/restart cycles (~$160k + near-cancelled fresh-produce contract) by cycling at the tempo of a noisy alarm system in a non-adversarial, minutes-to-hours environment — the specifying evidence (11 false alarms/30 days, redundant in-range sensor, flat 24h trend, clean lab results) sat unused until cycle four. The v6 routed run refused the trap at META: the tempo-mode classifier output DELIBERATE-BOUNDED (adversary none, dynamics min-to-h, trigger base rate 11/30) despite the deadline flag, and the routed m023 opportunity-cost pass (forgone-value check: ~$3k information vs ~$80k/cycle) + R4 m003 inversion (≥6 ranked categories incl. the cascade) + R3 m019 adversary pass (P(false|alarm) ≈ 0.9 → act-now is the risky move) produced the deliberate ~$3k play with a hard ≤45-min gate.
learning_signal: The tempo assumption has a precondition the style itself does not check: the environment must actually be fast and adversarial. Where dynamics are minutes-to-hours and the only pressure is the alert's salience, acting at the alarm's tempo means cycling at the false-alarm rate — a feedback loop the operator feeds. The corrective discipline is a META tempo-mode classifier (adversary present? dynamics timescale? action reversibility? trigger base rate) switching to DELIBERATE-BOUNDED, plus a base-rate statement for any salient signal and a wall-clock bound on the deliberation pass.
suggested_improvement: Keep the explicit tempo-mode classifier in META with inputs adversary-present / dynamics-timescale / reversibility / salience-vs-base-rate and outputs ACT-NOW | DELIBERATE-BOUNDED | PLAN; on guarantee signatures keep R4 m003 inversion and R3 m019 adversary pass as standing gates (on this case they are what make the deliberate play contract-complete); add to the WHY gate: no decision before collecting evidence whose collection cost is lower than the irreversible cost of the action.
